questions.q: What does Kelly say about the right time to start something?
a: About 99 percent of the time it is right now
Wait until you have saved enough money
Start only when you feel fully ready
The best moment was years ago
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists this among his ideas about timing.

questions.q: What does Kelly suggest doing when you feel like quitting?
a: Do five more
Take a long break
Change your goal entirely
Ask a mentor to decide
questions.why: Lesson 1 says five more will either keep you going or end on a high note.

questions.q: How does Kelly distinguish riches from wealth?
a: The rich have money; the wealthy have time
The rich have time; the wealthy have money
Both are measured by yearly income
Neither can be built slowly
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes his line about money, time and wealth.

questions.q: What does Kelly say about comparison?
a: It kills happiness, so compare with yesterday's you
It motivates people to work harder
It should be limited to close friends
It fades naturally with age
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls comparison the greatest killer of happiness.

questions.q: What does Kelly recommend giving away?
a: About ten percent of income for outsized happiness
Only what you expect to get back
Time instead of money whenever possible
Gifts given anonymously to avoid attention
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a small loss in purchasing power buys far more happiness.
